objects.description: 16-bit big-endian value stored in a flattened device tree (FDT) blob. Marked bitwise to help sparse/checker catch endian misuse. Convert with fdt16_to_cpu()/cpu_to_fdt16().
32-bit big-endian value stored in an FDT blob. Use fdt32_to_cpu()/cpu_to_fdt32() when reading/writing native values.
64-bit big-endian value stored in an FDT blob. Use fdt64_to_cpu()/cpu_to_fdt64() for endian conversion.
On-disk header for a flattened device tree blob. All fields are big-endian fdt32_t. Provides offsets/sizes for the blob’s sub-blocks and versioning info.
One entry in the memory reservation map of a DTB, indicating a reserved physical address range. Values are big-endian fdt64_t.
Structure block record for a begin-node tag in the DTB. Contains the tag and the NUL-terminated node name (including optional unit address). Used internally in the structure block layout.
Structure block record for a property in the DTB. Contains tag, data length, string-table offset of the name, followed by the property data bytes.

functions.name: fdt_offset_ptr
functions.signature: const void *fdt_offset_ptr(const void *fdt, int offset, unsigned int checklen);
functions.description: Return a pointer into the FDT structure block at the given byte offset, optionally ensuring that at least checklen bytes are available. Intended for low-level access; most users should prefer higher-level APIs.
requirements: fdt must point to a valid FDT blob header and layout suitable for reading (see fdt_check_header/fdt_check_full).
offset must be within the structure block; passing an out-of-range offset is an error.
checklen must not exceed the remaining bytes at offset; otherwise the function fails/returns NULL (per typical libfdt semantics).
Caller must treat the returned pointer as read-only memory within the blob.

functions.name: fdt_next_tag
functions.signature: uint32_t fdt_next_tag(const void *fdt, int offset, int *nextoffset);
functions.description: Read the next tag in the structure block at the given offset and return it, updating nextoffset to the following tag position. Useful for manual traversal of structure tags.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT for reading.
offset must point within the structure block to the start of a tag; otherwise behavior results in error progression via returned value/nextoffset as per libfdt internals.
nextoffset, if non-NULL, must be writable to receive the next offset.

functions.name: fdt_next_node
functions.signature: int fdt_next_node(const void *fdt, int offset, int *depth);
functions.description: Iterate to the next node in a pre-order walk of the tree from the given node or starting position. Optionally updates current depth.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
offset is the current node offset or -1 to start from the root (common libfdt pattern though not explicitly documented here).
depth, if non-NULL, must point to an int for in/out depth tracking; caller must initialize it appropriately for the first call per usual libfdt usage.

functions.name: fdt_first_subnode
functions.signature: int fdt_first_subnode(const void *fdt, int offset);
functions.description: Return the offset of the first direct subnode of the node at offset, or -FDT_ERR_NOTFOUND if none.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
offset must refer to an FDT_BEGIN_NODE tag (a node).

functions.name: fdt_next_subnode
functions.signature: int fdt_next_subnode(const void *fdt, int offset);
functions.description: After fdt_first_subnode(), iterate to the next direct subnode of the same parent. Returns -FDT_ERR_NOTFOUND when no more subnodes exist.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
offset must be the offset of a direct subnode previously obtained (i.e., valid node offset).

functions.name: fdt_header_size
functions.signature: size_t fdt_header_size(const void *fdt);
functions.description: Return the size in bytes of the DTB header of the provided blob’s version.
requirements: fdt must point to a valid FDT header.

functions.name: fdt_header_size_
functions.signature: size_t fdt_header_size_(uint32_t version);
functions.description: Internal helper returning the header size (in bytes) for a given devicetree version.
requirements: version must be a valid DTB version number recognized by libfdt.

functions.name: fdt_check_header
functions.signature: int fdt_check_header(const void *fdt);
functions.description: Sanity-check the FDT header to determine if the buffer appears to be a valid device tree with a consistent header.
requirements: fdt must point to a buffer at least large enough to contain an FDT header.
Caller must handle negative error codes: -FDT_ERR_BADMAGIC, -FDT_ERR_BADVERSION, -FDT_ERR_BADSTATE, -FDT_ERR_TRUNCATED.

functions.name: fdt_move
functions.signature: int fdt_move(const void *fdt, void *buf, int bufsize);
functions.description: Relocate an FDT blob to a (possibly overlapping) destination buffer, adjusting internal offsets as needed. Commonly used to move/resize a blob before modification.
requirements: fdt must point to a valid, readable FDT.
buf must point to a writable buffer of size bufsize bytes.
bufsize must be at least fdt_totalsize(fdt) to succeed; otherwise returns -FDT_ERR_NOSPACE.
Overlapping moves are allowed, including fdt == buf.

functions.name: fdt_check_full
functions.signature: int fdt_check_full(const void *fdt, size_t bufsize);
functions.description: Validate the entire FDT blob fits within bufsize and is well-formed, catching truncation and layout errors beyond the header.
requirements: fdt must point to the start of a buffer that contains an FDT.
bufsize must be the total size of the buffer containing the FDT.

functions.name: fdt_get_string
functions.signature: const char *fdt_get_string(const void *fdt, int stroffset, int *lenp);
functions.description: Return a pointer to a string in the strings block at the given offset, optionally returning its length in lenp.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
stroffset must be within the strings block and point to a valid NUL-terminated string.
lenp, if non-NULL, must be writable.

functions.name: fdt_string
functions.signature: const char *fdt_string(const void *fdt, int stroffset);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper to retrieve a string in the strings block by offset. Returns NULL if out of bounds or invalid.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
stroffset must be within the strings block and point to a valid NUL-terminated string.

functions.name: fdt_find_max_phandle
functions.signature: int fdt_find_max_phandle(const void *fdt, uint32_t *phandle);
functions.description: Scan the tree and return the highest valid phandle value found via the output parameter.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
phandle must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the maximum phandle on success.
Caller must check the return value; phandle is only valid if return is 0.

functions.name: fdt_get_max_phandle
functions.signature: static inline uint32_t fdt_get_max_phandle(const void *fdt);
functions.description: Deprecated helper that returns the highest phandle directly or -1 on error, ignoring invalid phandles (0, 0xffffffff).
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
Caller must check for return value (uint32_t)-1 to detect errors.

functions.name: fdt_generate_phandle
functions.signature: int fdt_generate_phandle(const void *fdt, uint32_t *phandle);
functions.description: Produce a new unused phandle value, one greater than the highest valid phandle in the tree.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
phandle must be non-NULL to receive the generated value.
Caller must check return code; output valid only on success.

functions.name: fdt_num_mem_rsv
functions.signature: int fdt_num_mem_rsv(const void *fdt);
functions.description: Return the number of non-terminating entries in the reservation map (excludes the terminating 0,0 and any expansion 0,0 entries).
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.

functions.name: fdt_get_mem_rsv
functions.signature: int fdt_get_mem_rsv(const void *fdt, int n, uint64_t *address, uint64_t *size);
functions.description: Fetch the nth reservation entry’s address and size in native endianness.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
n must be a non-negative index within the number of reservation entries.
address and size must be non-NULL pointers to receive the values.
Caller must handle standard negative error codes as documented.

functions.name: fdt_subnode_offset_namelen
functions.signature: int fdt_subnode_offset_namelen(const void *fdt, int parentoffset, const char *name, int namelen);
functions.description: Find the direct subnode of parentoffset whose name matches the first namelen characters of name (unit address matching rules apply).
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
parentoffset must refer to an FDT_BEGIN_NODE tag.
name must point to at least namelen bytes.
namelen must be non-negative.

functions.name: fdt_subnode_offset
functions.signature: int fdt_subnode_offset(const void *fdt, int parentoffset, const char *name);
functions.description: Find a direct subnode of the given parent by name. The provided name may include or omit a unit address; omission may be ambiguous.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
parentoffset must refer to an FDT_BEGIN_NODE tag.
name must be a valid string.

functions.name: fdt_path_offset_namelen
functions.signature: int fdt_path_offset_namelen(const void *fdt, const char *path, int namelen);
functions.description: Find a node by the first namelen characters of an absolute or alias-based path. Behaves like fdt_path_offset() but with substring length.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
path must point to at least namelen bytes representing a path; if not absolute, first component must be a valid alias.
namelen must be non-negative.

functions.name: fdt_path_offset
functions.signature: int fdt_path_offset(const void *fdt, const char *path);
functions.description: Resolve a node by full path. If not absolute, first component is resolved through /aliases. Unit-address omission in components may be ambiguous.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
path must be a valid string. If it does not start with '/', the first component must name a valid alias in /aliases.
Caller must handle negative libfdt error returns as documented.

functions.name: fdt_get_name
functions.signature: const char *fdt_get_name(const void *fdt, int nodeoffset, int *lenp);
functions.description: Return the name (including any unit address) of the node at nodeoffset, optionally returning its length via lenp.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
nodeoffset must point to an FDT_BEGIN_NODE tag.
lenp, if non-NULL, must be writable; on error it receives a negative error code.

functions.name: fdt_first_property_offset
functions.signature: int fdt_first_property_offset(const void *fdt, int nodeoffset);
functions.description: Return the offset of the first property of the node at nodeoffset, or -FDT_ERR_NOTFOUND if none.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
nodeoffset must refer to an FDT_BEGIN_NODE tag.

functions.name: fdt_next_property_offset
functions.signature: int fdt_next_property_offset(const void *fdt, int offset);
functions.description: Given a property offset, return the offset of the next property within the same node, or -FDT_ERR_NOTFOUND if none.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
offset must refer to an FDT_PROP tag.

functions.name: fdt_get_property_by_offset
functions.signature: const struct fdt_property *fdt_get_property_by_offset(const void *fdt, int offset, int *lenp);
functions.description: Return a pointer to the fdt_property at the given structure offset and optionally its value length via lenp. Only works for DTB version >= 16.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT (version >= 16 for this API).
offset must refer to an FDT_PROP tag.
lenp, if non-NULL, must be writable; on error it receives a negative error code.
Returned pointer points into the blob; do not modify when using const variant.

functions.name: fdt_get_property_namelen
functions.signature: const struct fdt_property *fdt_get_property_namelen(const void *fdt, int nodeoffset, const char *name, int namelen, int *lenp);
functions.description: Find a property in a node by matching only the first namelen characters of name. Returns the fdt_property pointer if found.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
nodeoffset must refer to an FDT_BEGIN_NODE tag.
name must point to at least namelen bytes; namelen must be non-negative.
lenp, if non-NULL, must be writable for value length or error code.

functions.name: fdt_get_property
functions.signature: const struct fdt_property *fdt_get_property(const void *fdt, int nodeoffset, const char *name, int *lenp);
functions.description: Locate a named property in the node and return its fdt_property pointer; optionally return the value length via lenp.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
nodeoffset must refer to an FDT_BEGIN_NODE tag.
name must be a valid string.
lenp, if non-NULL, must be writable; on error it receives a negative error code.

functions.name: fdt_getprop_by_offset
functions.signature: const void *fdt_getprop_by_offset(const void *fdt, int offset, const char **namep, int *lenp);
functions.description: Return a pointer to the value of the property at the given property offset, plus optionally its length and name pointer into the strings block.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
offset must refer to an FDT_PROP tag.
namep, if non-NULL, must be writable to receive a pointer to the name within the strings block.
lenp, if non-NULL, must be writable; on error it receives a negative error code.
Returned value pointer is into the blob; do not modify.

functions.name: fdt_getprop_namelen
functions.signature: const void *fdt_getprop_namelen(const void *fdt, int nodeoffset, const char *name, int namelen, int *lenp);
functions.description: Return a pointer to the value of a property whose name matches the first namelen characters of name within the specified node.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
nodeoffset must refer to an FDT_BEGIN_NODE tag.
name must point to at least namelen bytes; namelen must be non-negative.
lenp, if non-NULL, must be writable; on error it receives a negative error code.
Returned pointer is into the blob.

functions.name: fdt_getprop
functions.signature: const void *fdt_getprop(const void *fdt, int nodeoffset, const char *name, int *lenp);
functions.description: Return a pointer to the value of a named property in a node, optionally returning its length via lenp.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
nodeoffset must refer to an FDT_BEGIN_NODE tag.
name must be a valid string.
lenp, if non-NULL, must be writable; on error it receives a negative error code.
Returned pointer is into the blob.

functions.name: fdt_get_phandle
functions.signature: uint32_t fdt_get_phandle(const void *fdt, int nodeoffset);
functions.description: Return the phandle value of the node at nodeoffset, or 0 if none or on error.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
nodeoffset must refer to a node (FDT_BEGIN_NODE).
Caller must treat 0 as no phandle or error.

functions.name: fdt_get_alias_namelen
functions.signature: const char *fdt_get_alias_namelen(const void *fdt, const char *name, int namelen);
functions.description: Return the expansion (target path) of an alias whose name matches the first namelen characters of name, or NULL if not found.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
/aliases node should exist for non-NULL results.
name must point to at least namelen bytes; namelen must be non-negative.

functions.name: fdt_get_alias
functions.signature: const char *fdt_get_alias(const void *fdt, const char *name);
functions.description: Return the path expansion of the alias named name from the /aliases node, or NULL if absent.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
name must be a valid string.
/aliases node should exist for successful lookup.

functions.name: fdt_get_symbol_namelen
functions.signature: const char *fdt_get_symbol_namelen(const void *fdt, const char *name, int namelen);
functions.description: Return the expansion (target path) of a symbol whose name matches the first namelen characters of name from /__symbols__, or NULL if not found.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT built with -@ (having /__symbols__).
name must point to at least namelen bytes; namelen must be non-negative.

functions.name: fdt_get_symbol
functions.signature: const char *fdt_get_symbol(const void *fdt, const char *name);
functions.description: Return the path referenced by a symbol property in /__symbols__ whose name equals name. Requires a blob compiled with dtc -@.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT with /__symbols__ present.
name must be a valid string.

functions.name: fdt_get_path
functions.signature: int fdt_get_path(const void *fdt, int nodeoffset, char *buf, int buflen);
functions.description: Compute the absolute path of the node at nodeoffset and store it as a NUL-terminated string in buf.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
nodeoffset must refer to an FDT_BEGIN_NODE tag.
buf must be a writable buffer of size buflen bytes; it must be large enough to hold the path plus NUL or -FDT_ERR_NOSPACE is returned.
This function is O(tree) relative to node position and is expensive.

functions.name: fdt_supernode_atdepth_offset
functions.signature: int fdt_supernode_atdepth_offset(const void *fdt, int nodeoffset, int supernodedepth, int *nodedepth);
functions.description: Return the ancestor of nodeoffset at the specified depth from root. Optionally return the actual depth of nodeoffset via nodedepth.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
nodeoffset must refer to an FDT_BEGIN_NODE tag.
supernodedepth must be >= 0 and <= depth(nodeoffset) or -FDT_ERR_NOTFOUND is returned.
nodedepth, if non-NULL, must be writable.
This function is expensive (scans from start).

functions.name: fdt_node_depth
functions.signature: int fdt_node_depth(const void *fdt, int nodeoffset);
functions.description: Return the depth (root=0) of the node at nodeoffset.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
nodeoffset must refer to an FDT_BEGIN_NODE tag.
This function is expensive (scans from start).

functions.name: fdt_parent_offset
functions.signature: int fdt_parent_offset(const void *fdt, int nodeoffset);
functions.description: Return the offset of the parent node of the node at nodeoffset.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
nodeoffset must refer to an FDT_BEGIN_NODE tag.
This function is expensive (scans from start twice).

functions.name: fdt_node_offset_by_prop_value
functions.signature: int fdt_node_offset_by_prop_value(const void *fdt, int startoffset, const char *propname, const void *propval, int proplen);
functions.description: Find the first node after startoffset whose property propname equals the given value (propval of length proplen). Use -1 to include the root.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
propname must be a valid string.
propval must point to at least proplen bytes; proplen may be zero.
startoffset should be -1 for including root; otherwise must be a valid node offset.

functions.name: fdt_node_offset_by_phandle
functions.signature: int fdt_node_offset_by_phandle(const void *fdt, uint32_t phandle);
functions.description: Return the node offset of the node with the given phandle value.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
phandle must not be 0 or 0xffffffff (-1 as uint32_t), else -FDT_ERR_BADPHANDLE.
Tree must not contain duplicate phandles; otherwise results are undefined.

functions.name: fdt_node_check_compatible
functions.signature: int fdt_node_check_compatible(const void *fdt, int nodeoffset, const char *compatible);
functions.description: Check whether the node has a 'compatible' property containing the given string. Returns 0 if match, 1 if property exists but does not match, or negative error.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
nodeoffset must refer to an FDT_BEGIN_NODE tag.
compatible must be a valid string.

functions.name: fdt_node_offset_by_compatible
functions.signature: int fdt_node_offset_by_compatible(const void *fdt, int startoffset, const char *compatible);
functions.description: Find the first node after startoffset whose 'compatible' property contains the given string. Use -1 to include the root.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
compatible must be a valid string.
startoffset should be -1 to include root; otherwise must be a valid node offset.

functions.name: fdt_stringlist_contains
functions.signature: int fdt_stringlist_contains(const char *strlist, int listlen, const char *str);
functions.description: Check whether a NUL-separated string list contains the given string.
requirements: strlist must point to a buffer of length listlen bytes representing a string list (one or more NUL-terminated strings).
str must be a valid string to search for.
Returns 1 if found, 0 if not found or invalid list.

functions.name: fdt_stringlist_count
functions.signature: int fdt_stringlist_count(const void *fdt, int nodeoffset, const char *property);
functions.description: Count the number of strings in a NUL-separated string list property in the given node.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
nodeoffset must refer to an FDT_BEGIN_NODE tag.
property must be a valid property name string.
Caller must handle -FDT_ERR_BADVALUE for non-NUL-terminated property and -FDT_ERR_NOTFOUND if property missing.

functions.name: fdt_stringlist_search
functions.signature: int fdt_stringlist_search(const void *fdt, int nodeoffset, const char *property, const char *string);
functions.description: Search a string list property for the given string and return its index if found.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
nodeoffset must refer to an FDT_BEGIN_NODE tag.
property and string must be valid strings.
Caller must handle -FDT_ERR_BADVALUE for non-NUL-terminated property and -FDT_ERR_NOTFOUND if missing or not containing the string.

functions.name: fdt_stringlist_get
functions.signature: const char *fdt_stringlist_get(const void *fdt, int nodeoffset, const char *property, int index, int *lenp);
functions.description: Return a pointer to the string at the specified index within a string list property, optionally returning its length via lenp.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
nodeoffset must refer to an FDT_BEGIN_NODE tag.
property must be a valid string property name.
index must be a non-negative index within the number of strings.
lenp, if non-NULL, must be writable; on failure it receives a negative error code.
Property may be non-NUL-terminated; this function can still return strings (e.g., empty string in small cell properties).

functions.name: fdt_address_cells
functions.signature: int fdt_address_cells(const void *fdt, int nodeoffset);
functions.description: Return the #address-cells value for the given node if present and valid. Defaults to 2 if missing.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
nodeoffset must refer to an FDT_BEGIN_NODE tag.
Caller must handle -FDT_ERR_BADNCELLS when the property is badly formatted/invalid.

functions.name: fdt_size_cells
functions.signature: int fdt_size_cells(const void *fdt, int nodeoffset);
functions.description: Return the #size-cells value for the given node if present and valid. Defaults to 1 if missing.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT.
nodeoffset must refer to an FDT_BEGIN_NODE tag.
Caller must handle -FDT_ERR_BADNCELLS when the property is badly formatted/invalid.

functions.name: fdt_setprop_inplace_namelen_partial
functions.signature: int fdt_setprop_inplace_namelen_partial(void *fdt, int nodeoffset, const char *name, int namelen, uint32_t idx, const void *val, int len);
functions.description: Overwrite a portion (starting at element index idx) of an existing property’s value in-place without changing its total size, matching property name by the first namelen characters.
requirements: fdt must be a valid, writable FDT.
nodeoffset must refer to an FDT_BEGIN_NODE tag.
The property identified by the (partial) name must exist and have the same total length as implied; this call cannot change property size.
name must point to at least namelen bytes; namelen must be non-negative.
val must point to len bytes to write.
idx selects the start offset within an array-like property; caller must ensure idx/len fit within the existing property length.
Returns negative libfdt error on failure.

functions.name: fdt_setprop_inplace
functions.signature: int fdt_setprop_inplace(void *fdt, int nodeoffset, const char *name, const void *val, int len);
functions.description: Replace an existing property’s value in-place with val of length len. Property size must not change.
requirements: fdt must be a valid, writable FDT.
nodeoffset must refer to an FDT_BEGIN_NODE tag.
Property name must exist and have current length equal to len, otherwise -FDT_ERR_NOSPACE is returned.
val must point to at least len bytes.

functions.name: fdt_nop_property
functions.signature: int fdt_nop_property(void *fdt, int nodeoffset, const char *name);
functions.description: Replace a named property in the node with FDT_NOP tags, effectively removing it, without moving other parts of the tree.
requirements: fdt must be a valid, writable FDT.
nodeoffset must refer to an FDT_BEGIN_NODE tag.
name must be a valid string of an existing property to nop.

functions.name: fdt_nop_node
functions.signature: int fdt_nop_node(void *fdt, int nodeoffset);
functions.description: Replace a node and its subtree with FDT_NOP tags, effectively removing it from the tree, without moving other parts of the tree.
requirements: fdt must be a valid, writable FDT.
nodeoffset must refer to an FDT_BEGIN_NODE tag.

functions.name: fdt_create_with_flags
functions.signature: int fdt_create_with_flags(void *buf, int bufsize, uint32_t flags);
functions.description: Begin creation of a new FDT in the provided buffer using the sequential write API, honoring creation flags.
requirements: buf must point to a writable buffer of size bufsize.
bufsize must be sufficient for a minimal FDT or -FDT_ERR_NOSPACE is returned.
flags must be a valid combination of FDT_CREATE_FLAG_* (or 0); otherwise -FDT_ERR_BADFLAGS.
Creation must be finalized with fdt_finish() to produce a valid FDT.

functions.name: fdt_create
functions.signature: int fdt_create(void *buf, int bufsize);
functions.description: Begin creation of a new FDT in the provided buffer with default flags (equivalent to fdt_create_with_flags(buf, bufsize, 0)).
requirements: buf must point to a writable buffer of size bufsize sufficient for a minimal FDT.
Caller must complete the sequence (reservemap, nodes, properties) and call fdt_finish().

functions.name: fdt_resize
functions.signature: int fdt_resize(void *fdt, void *buf, int bufsize);
functions.description: Internal/sequence helper to resize or move the in-construction FDT to a new buffer/size during sequential creation.
requirements: fdt must point to a valid sequential-write FDT under construction.
buf must be a writable buffer of size bufsize.
May change internal offsets; caller should continue using the returned/updated buffer.

functions.name: fdt_add_reservemap_entry
functions.signature: int fdt_add_reservemap_entry(void *fdt, uint64_t addr, uint64_t size);
functions.description: During sequential creation, add a reservation map entry with the given address and size.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT under sequential creation.
addr and size are 64-bit values for the reserved region; size may be zero to mark termination in raw map but here adds an entry.
Sufficient space must exist or -FDT_ERR_NOSPACE is returned.

functions.name: fdt_finish_reservemap
functions.signature: int fdt_finish_reservemap(void *fdt);
functions.description: Terminate the reservation map during sequential creation. After this, structure creation can begin.
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT under sequential creation.
Must be called after all reservation entries are added and before beginning nodes/properties.

functions.name: fdt_begin_node
functions.signature: int fdt_begin_node(void *fdt, const char *name);
functions.description: Begin a new node in the sequential write API with the given name (including optional unit address).
requirements: fdt must be a valid FDT under sequential creation.
name must be a valid string for the node name (including any unit address).
Nodes must be properly nested and later closed with fdt_end_node().

functions.name: fdt_property
functions.signature: int fdt_property(void *fdt, const char *name, const void *val, int len);
functions.description: Add a property with the given name and value to the current node while sequentially writing the FDT.

import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator produces a valid, minimal DTB (Flattened Device Tree Blob)
# with a root node, an /aliases node, a compatible property, string list
# properties, and some common properties. This aims to satisfy libfdt readers
# and provide content that exercises lookups by name, partial name, stringlist
# operations, and RW operations in the fuzz stubs.
#
# The DTB layout:
# [fdt_header][reserve_map][structure_block][strings_block]
# Structure block contains tags: BEGIN_NODE, PROP, END_NODE, ... and ends with END.
# All integer header/fields are big-endian.
# Strings block contains NUL-terminated strings for property names.
#
# We vary content by seed: node names, properties, aliases, and string lists.

FDT_MAGIC = 0xd00dfeed
FDT_BEGIN_NODE = 0x1
FDT_END_NODE = 0x2
FDT_PROP = 0x3
FDT_NOP = 0x4
FDT_END = 0x9

# Header version 17+ includes size_dt_struct; we use version 17 for simplicity
DT_VERSION = 17
LAST_COMP_VERSION = 16


def be32(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">I", x & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def be64(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">Q", x & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)


def pad4(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    rem = (-len(b)) & 3
    if rem:
        return b + b"\x00" * rem
    return b


def sbegin_node(name: str) -> bytes:
    # BEGIN_NODE tag + name (NUL-terminated), padded to 4
    data = be32(FDT_BEGIN_NODE)
    nb = name.encode("utf-8") + b"\x00"
    data += pad4(nb)
    return data


def send_node() -> bytes:
    return be32(FDT_END_NODE)


def sprop(nameoff: int, val: bytes) -> bytes:
    # PROP tag + len + nameoff + value padded
    data = be32(FDT_PROP)
    data += be32(len(val))
    data += be32(nameoff)
    data += pad4(val)
    return data


def send_struct() -> bytes:
    return be32(FDT_END)


def make_strings_table(strings: List[str]) -> Tuple[bytes, dict]:
    # Build a unique, deterministic strings block, returning block and name->offset map
    offmap = {}
    blob = bytearray()
    cur = 0
    for s in strings:
        if s in offmap:
            continue
        sb = s.encode("utf-8") + b"\x00"
        offmap[s] = cur
        blob.extend(sb)
        cur += len(sb)
    return bytes(blob), offmap


def choose(lst: List[str], rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    return lst[rnd.randrange(len(lst))]


def make_stringlist(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # NUL-separated list as property value
    if not strings:
        return b"\x00"  # empty string list edge case
    return b"\x00".join(s.encode("utf-8") for s in strings) + b"\x00"


def build_dtb(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Vary names and content
    compat_bases = [
        "vendor,devA", "acme,widget", "test,board", "foo,bar", "linux,testdev"
    ]
    root_name = "/"  # root node has empty name in struct; but libfdt often uses BEGIN_NODE with empty name

    # Strings used as property names
    prop_names = [
        "compatible", "model", "name", "status", "device_type",
        "phandle", "#address-cells", "#size-cells", "reg",
        "label", "aliases", "clock-names", "clocks", "ranges",
        "my-prop", "stringlist", "empty", "data"
    ]

    # Generate content
    compat_list = [choose(compat_bases, rnd)]
    # Sometimes include stringlist with multiple entries
    extra_compat = ["vendor,alt" + str(rnd.randrange(3)) for _ in range(rnd.randrange(0, 2))]
    compat_list.extend(extra_compat)

    model_val = f"model-{rnd.randrange(1000)}"
    status_val = choose(["okay", "disabled"], rnd)

    # Common DT layout: root with address-cells/size-cells; child node with unit address; aliases node
    addr_cells = choose([1, 2, 3], rnd)  # 1 or 2 are common; 3 is edge-case but still valid for readers
    size_cells = choose([1, 2], rnd)

    child_unit = rnd.randrange(0, 4)
    child_name = f"node{child_unit}@{child_unit * 0x1000:x}"

    # Aliases
    alias_name = choose(["serial0", "ethernet0", "spi0", "i2c0", "uart0"], rnd)
    alias_target = f"/{child_name}"

    # Clock names stringlist
    clock_names = ["clk0", "core", "bus"][: rnd.randrange(1, 4)]

    # Build strings block entries needed
    needed_strings = set(prop_names)
    needed_strings.update(["compatible", "model", "status", "#address-cells", "#size-cells",
                           "reg", "clock-names", alias_name])
    # Include some random property names for fdt_* lookups
    for _ in range(rnd.randrange(2, 6)):
        needed_strings.add(f"prop{rnd.randrange(100)}")

    strings_blob, nameoff = make_strings_table(sorted(needed_strings))

    # Build structure block
    struct_blob = bytearray()

    # Root node: name is empty string, but some producers put empty; we use empty per spec
    struct_blob.extend(be32(FDT_BEGIN_NODE))
    struct_blob.extend(pad4(b"\x00"))

    # Root properties
    struct_blob.extend(sprop(nameoff["compatible"], make_stringlist(compat_list)))
    struct_blob.extend(sprop(nameoff["model"], model_val.encode("utf-8") + b"\x00"))
    struct_blob.extend(sprop(nameoff["status"], status_val.encode("utf-8") + b"\x00"))

    # address/size cells (32-bit big-endian integers)
    struct_blob.extend(sprop(nameoff["#address-cells"], be32(addr_cells)))
    struct_blob.extend(sprop(nameoff["#size-cells"], be32(size_cells)))

    # clock-names stringlist
    struct_blob.extend(sprop(nameoff["clock-names"], make_stringlist(clock_names)))

    # /aliases node
    struct_blob.extend(sbegin_node("aliases"))
    # alias property value is path string to target
    struct_blob.extend(sprop(nameoff[alias_name], alias_target.encode("utf-8") + b"\x00"))
    struct_blob.extend(send_node())

    # Child node with unit address and simple properties
    struct_blob.extend(sbegin_node(child_name))

    # reg property: array of cells: addr_cells + size_cells, 32-bit big-endian words
    reg_cells = []
    # Compose address and size values
    addr_val = rnd.randrange(0, 0x100000)
    size_val = rnd.randrange(0x100, 0x2000)
    def cells_from_u64(v: int, cells: int) -> List[int]:
        out = []
        # split into 32-bit cells big-endian order
        for i in range(cells):
            shift = 32 * (cells - 1 - i)
            out.append((v >> shift) & 0xFFFFFFFF)
        return out
    reg_cells.extend(cells_from_u64(addr_val, addr_cells))
    reg_cells.extend(cells_from_u64(size_val, size_cells))
    reg_bytes = b"".join(be32(c) for c in reg_cells)
    struct_blob.extend(sprop(nameoff["reg"], reg_bytes))

    # arbitrary stringlist property
    stringlist_vals = [f"val{rnd.randrange(5)}" for _ in range(rnd.randrange(1, 4))]
    struct_blob.extend(sprop(nameoff["stringlist"], make_stringlist(stringlist_vals)))

    # an empty property (len=0) named "empty"
    struct_blob.extend(sprop(nameoff["empty"], b""))

    # some random data property
    data_len = rnd.randrange(0, 16)
    data_bytes = bytes(rnd.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(data_len))
    struct_blob.extend(sprop(nameoff["data"], data_bytes))

    struct_blob.extend(send_node())  # end child

    # End of structure
    struct_blob.extend(send_struct())

    struct_blob = bytes(struct_blob)

    # Reserve map: at least a terminating (0,0)
    rsvmap = be64(0) + be64(0)

    # Header sizes and offsets
    off_mem_rsvmap = struct.calcsize(">IIIIIIIIIII")  # header size for v17
    # But header size varies with version; compute via helper
    header_size = 0
    def header_size_for_version(v: int) -> int:
        # v1: up to last_comp_version
        # v2: + boot_cpuid_phys
        # v3: + size_dt_strings
        # v17: + size_dt_struct
        # Minimal sizes by version
        if v < 2:
            return struct.calcsize(">IIIIIII")
        if v < 3:
            return struct.calcsize(">IIIIIIII")
        if v < 17:
            return struct.calcsize(">IIIIIIIII")
        return struct.calcsize(">IIIIIIIIIII")
    header_size = header_size_for_version(DT_VERSION)

    # Compute offsets with header first, then rsvmap, then struct, then strings
    off_dt_struct = header_size + len(rsvmap)
    off_dt_strings = off_dt_struct + len(struct_blob)

    size_dt_struct = len(struct_blob)
    size_dt_strings = len(strings_blob)

    totalsize = off_dt_strings + size_dt_strings

    # Build header
    hdr = bytearray()
    hdr.extend(be32(FDT_MAGIC))
    hdr.extend(be32(totalsize))
    hdr.extend(be32(off_dt_struct))
    hdr.extend(be32(off_dt_strings))
    hdr.extend(be32(header_size))  # off_mem_rsvmap stored here per struct fdt_header
    hdr.extend(be32(DT_VERSION))
    hdr.extend(be32(LAST_COMP_VERSION))
    hdr.extend(be32(0))  # boot_cpuid_phys
    hdr.extend(be32(size_dt_strings))
    hdr.extend(be32(size_dt_struct))

    blob = bytes(hdr) + rsvmap + struct_blob + strings_blob

    # Ensure total size matches header
    blob = blob[:totalsize]

    # The fuzzing harness expects attributes like is_valid/off_dt_struct etc.
    # Some harnesses derive attributes internally; we cannot set them directly in bytes,
    # but providing a valid DTB with correct offsets should make checks pass.

    # Limit size as requested
    if len(blob) > 4096:
        blob = blob[:4096]

    return blob


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    return build_dtb(rnd)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces a valid identifier string suitable for libfdt alias/symbol
# lookups (no slashes, NUL-terminated when passed as bytes by the fuzzer infra).
# We bias generation toward common and interesting alias/symbol naming patterns
# used in device trees so that lookups are likely to hit when the DT contains
# matching entries (e.g., aliases: serial0, ethernet0, i2c0; symbols: node@addr,
# label references with dots/underscores, etc.).

ALNUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
ID_EXTRA = ",._+-"  # Allowed extra characters typically seen in DT identifiers
ID_CHARS = ALNUM + ID_EXTRA

COMMON_PREFIXES = [
    "serial", "uart", "ethernet", "eth", "i2c", "spi", "mmc", "sd", "sdhci",
    "gpio", "pwm", "usb", "pcie", "sata", "rtc", "watchdog", "wdt",
    "can", "mipi", "dsi", "dpi", "dp", "hdmi", "audio", "snd", "sound",
    "led", "leds", "phy", "phylink", "mdio", "nand", "qspi", "psci",
    "cpu", "cpus", "l2", "crypto", "rng", "dma", "irq", "intc", "timer",
    "sram", "dram", "mem", "memory", "nvme", "sdio", "bluetooth", "bt",
]

COMMON_SUFFIX_INDEXED = ["0", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6", "7"]

# Fragments to compose dot/underscore variants often used in symbol names
DOT_SEGMENTS = [
    "clk", "reset", "supply", "reg", "ctrl", "core", "bus", "host", "device",
    "tx", "rx", "in", "out", "hs", "fs", "ls", "phy", "pll", "mux",
]

UNDERSCORE_SEGMENTS = [
    "default", "fast", "slow", "boot", "backup", "primary", "secondary",
]

# Some realistic unit-address like fragments (though slashes are not used in identifiers)
UNIT_ADDR_HEX = [
    "00", "10", "20", "30", "40", "50", "60", "70", "80", "90", "a0", "b0", "c0", "d0", "e0", "f0",
]


def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 48) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Ensure first char is letter or underscore to match common identifier rules
    first_choices = string.ascii_letters + "_"
    s = [rng.choice(first_choices)]
    while len(s) < n:
        s.append(rng.choice(ID_CHARS))
    return "".join(s)


def _make_alias_style(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Patterns like: serial0, ethernet1, i2c2, spi0.0 (without dot usually for alias)
    base = rng.choice(COMMON_PREFIXES)
    # 70%: simple base+index; 20%: base + index + extra; 10%: plain base
    roll = rng.random()
    if roll < 0.7:
        return base + rng.choice(COMMON_SUFFIX_INDEXED)
    elif roll < 0.9:
        extra = rng.choice(["_", ",", "+", "-"])
        return base + rng.choice(COMMON_SUFFIX_INDEXED) + extra + rng.choice(ALNUM)
    else:
        return base


def _make_symbol_style(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Symbols often look like labels or node-like names without slashes, e.g.:
    # uart0, spi0_cs0, phy0, cpu0, pcie@10000000 (without slash), clk.core, gpioA_0
    base = rng.choice(COMMON_PREFIXES)
    parts: List[str] = []
    # Optional unit-address fragment with '@' is allowed in identifiers, but many
    # libfdt symbol/alias names avoid '@'. We'll include occasionally.
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # base + index
        parts.append(base + rng.choice(COMMON_SUFFIX_INDEXED))
    else:
        parts.append(base)
    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        # Append unit-address like portion
        parts[-1] += "@" + rng.choice(UNIT_ADDR_HEX)
    # Optionally add dot or underscore segments
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(rng.choice(DOT_SEGMENTS))
        name = ".".join(parts)
    elif rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(rng.choice(UNDERSCORE_SEGMENTS))
        name = "_".join(parts)
    else:
        name = parts[0]
    return name


def _mix_cases(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    # Randomly vary case for a subset to explore case-sensitive spaces
    out = []
    for ch in s:
        if ch.isalpha() and rng.random() < 0.2:
            out.append(ch.upper() if ch.islower() else ch.lower())
        else:
            out.append(ch)
    return "".join(out)


def _ensure_length_bounds(s: str) -> str:
    # Enforce a practical bound so resulting bytes fit under 4096 comfortably
    if len(s) > 256:
        return s[:256]
    return s


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a strategy to generate identifiers with different distributions
    strategy = rng.random()
    if strategy < 0.45:
        s = _make_alias_style(rng)
    elif strategy < 0.9:
        s = _make_symbol_style(rng)
    else:
        # Fully random but valid identifier token
        s = _rand_ident(rng, 1, 48)

    # Occasionally augment with additional allowed characters segments
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        # Append a small extra token separated by one of the allowed punctuation
        sep = rng.choice([",", ".", "_", "+", "-"])
        tail = _rand_ident(rng, 1, rng.randint(2, 8))
        # For dot-separated, avoid starting tail with punctuation
        s = s + sep + tail

    # Occasionally add numeric tail
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        s += str(rng.randint(0, 99))

    s = _mix_cases(rng, s)
    s = _ensure_length_bounds(s)

    # Return as bytes; fuzzer infra will treat as a NUL-terminated C-string by
    # providing the buffer to functions expecting const char*.
    return s.encode("ascii", errors="ignore")

import random
import struct
import sys

# This generator produces a valid Flattened Device Tree (DTB) blob (FDT)
# with common nodes and properties, so libfdt functions operating on:
# - property searches by value/name
# - in-place property updates
# - sequential property creation (when the harness is in seq mode)
# have meaningful inputs. The same buffer is supplied to FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls;
# we therefore place useful ASCII strings in the strings block, and provide
# diverse property values (strings, cells, address/size arrays, byte blobs).
#
# DTB layout (all big-endian):
# [header][reserve map][structure block][strings block]
# We build a small tree:
# /
#   compatible = "test,root";
#   model = "fuzz-device";
#   aliases { serial0 = "/soc/serial@1000"; eth0 = "/soc/ethernet@2000"; };
#   __symbols__ { uart0 = "/soc/serial@1000"; mac0 = "/soc/ethernet@2000"; };
#   chosen { bootargs = "console=ttyS0,115200"; };
#   soc {
#     #address-cells = <2>;
#     #size-cells = <1>;
#     serial@1000 { compatible = "ns16550"; reg = <0x0 0x1000 0x100>; phandle = <1>; status = "okay"; };
#     ethernet@2000 { compatible = "fuzz,net"; reg = <0x0 0x2000 0x1000>; local-mac-address = [52 54 00 12 34 56]; phandle = <2>; };
#   };
#   memory@80000000 { device_type = "memory"; reg = <0x0 0x80000000 0x2000000>; };
#
# We add multiple names and values to exercise name/namelen and value searches.
# The tree is aligned to 4-byte boundaries as per DTB spec. Totalsize <= 4096.

FDT_MAGIC = 0xd00dfeed
FDT_BEGIN_NODE = 0x1
FDT_END_NODE = 0x2
FDT_PROP = 0x3
FDT_NOP = 0x4
FDT_END = 0x9

DT_VERSION = 17  # use v17 so size_dt_struct is present


def be32(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">I", x & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def be64(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">Q", x & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)


def align4(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    pad = (-len(b)) & 3
    if pad:
        return b + (b"\x00" * pad)
    return b


def strz(s: str) -> bytes:
    return s.encode("utf-8") + b"\x00"


def prop(nameoff: int, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    # struct fdt_property { tag, len, nameoff, data[] }, all 4-byte aligned
    body = be32(FDT_PROP) + be32(len(data)) + be32(nameoff) + data
    return align4(body)


def begin_node(name: str) -> bytes:
    return align4(be32(FDT_BEGIN_NODE) + strz(name))


def end_node() -> bytes:
    return be32(FDT_END_NODE)


def end_struct() -> bytes:
    return be32(FDT_END)


def cells32(*vals: int) -> bytes:
    return b"".join(be32(v) for v in vals)


def gen_mac(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # locally administered unicast
    b0 = 0x02
    rest = [rng.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(5)]
    return bytes([b0] + rest)


def build_strings_table(strings: list[str]) -> tuple[bytes, dict[str, int]]:
    # Build a string block with unique strings, return blob and name->offset map
    blob = bytearray()
    offsets = {}
    for s in strings:
        if s in offsets:
            continue
        offsets[s] = len(blob)
        blob += strz(s)
    return bytes(blob), offsets


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Select some variability to cover different search values and sizes
    compat_root_choices = [
        "test,root",
        "acme,root",
        "demo,root",
    ]
    compat_soc_serial = ["ns16550", "snps,dw-apb-uart", "arm,pl011"]
    compat_eth = ["fuzz,net", "virtio,net", "smsc,lan9118"]

    root_compat = rng.choice(compat_root_choices)
    uart_compat = rng.choice(compat_soc_serial)
    eth_compat = rng.choice(compat_eth)

    mac = gen_mac(rng)

    # Strings we will reference in properties
    strings_pool = [
        "compatible",
        "model",
        "status",
        "reg",
        "phandle",
        "device_type",
        "local-mac-address",
        "bootargs",
        "#address-cells",
        "#size-cells",
        "serial0",
        "eth0",
        "uart0",
        "mac0",
        "aliases",
        "__symbols__",
        "chosen",
        "soc",
        f"{root_compat}",
        "fuzz-device",
        "okay",
        "memory",
        f"{uart_compat}",
        f"{eth_compat}",
        "console=ttyS0,115200",
        "serial@1000",
        "ethernet@2000",
        "memory@80000000",
    ]

    # Build strings block and map
    strings_blob, nameoff = build_strings_table(strings_pool)

    # Helper to get nameoff safely
    def no(s: str) -> int:
        return nameoff[s]

    # Build structure block
    st = bytearray()

    # Root node
    st += begin_node("")
    st += prop(no("compatible"), strz(root_compat))
    st += prop(no("model"), strz("fuzz-device"))

    # aliases
    st += begin_node("aliases")
    st += prop(no("serial0"), strz("/soc/serial@1000"))
    st += prop(no("eth0"), strz("/soc/ethernet@2000"))
    st += end_node()

    # __symbols__ to exercise symbol lookups
    st += begin_node("__symbols__")
    st += prop(no("uart0"), strz("/soc/serial@1000"))
    st += prop(no("mac0"), strz("/soc/ethernet@2000"))
    st += end_node()

    # chosen
    st += begin_node("chosen")
    st += prop(no("bootargs"), strz("console=ttyS0,115200"))
    st += end_node()

    # soc bus with address/size cells
    st += begin_node("soc")
    st += prop(no("#address-cells"), cells32(2))
    st += prop(no("#size-cells"), cells32(1))

    # serial@1000
    st += begin_node("serial@1000")
    st += prop(no("compatible"), strz(uart_compat))
    # reg: <0x0 0x1000 0x100>
    st += prop(no("reg"), cells32(0x0, 0x1000, 0x100))
    st += prop(no("phandle"), cells32(1))
    st += prop(no("status"), strz("okay"))
    st += end_node()

    # ethernet@2000
    st += begin_node("ethernet@2000")
    st += prop(no("compatible"), strz(eth_compat))
    # reg: <0x0 0x2000 0x1000>
    st += prop(no("reg"), cells32(0x0, 0x2000, 0x1000))
    st += prop(no("local-mac-address"), mac)
    st += prop(no("phandle"), cells32(2))
    st += end_node()

    st += end_node()  # end soc

    # memory node
    st += begin_node("memory@80000000")
    st += prop(no("device_type"), strz("memory"))
    st += prop(no("reg"), cells32(0x0, 0x80000000, 0x02000000))
    st += end_node()

    # end of structure
    st += end_struct()

    struct_block = bytes(st)
    struct_block = align4(struct_block)
    strings_block = align4(strings_blob)

    # Reservation map: none, just terminator {0,0}
    rsvmap = be64(0) + be64(0)

    # Header fields and offsets
    off_dt_struct = 0  # to be filled after header size known
    off_dt_strings = 0
    off_mem_rsvmap = 0

    # Compute header size for version 17: struct fdt_header up to size_dt_struct
    # libfdt uses 10 fdt32 fields for v17
    header_size = 10 * 4

    off_mem_rsvmap = header_size
    off_dt_struct = off_mem_rsvmap + len(rsvmap)
    off_dt_strings = off_dt_struct + len(struct_block)

    totalsize = off_dt_strings + len(strings_block)

    # Build header
    hdr = bytearray()
    hdr += be32(FDT_MAGIC)
    hdr += be32(totalsize)
    hdr += be32(off_dt_struct)
    hdr += be32(off_dt_strings)
    hdr += be32(off_mem_rsvmap)
    hdr += be32(DT_VERSION)
    hdr += be32(16)  # last_comp_version
    hdr += be32(0)   # boot_cpuid_phys
    hdr += be32(len(strings_block))  # size_dt_strings
    hdr += be32(len(struct_block))   # size_dt_struct

    blob = bytes(hdr) + rsvmap + struct_block + strings_block

    # Safety: ensure size within limit
    if len(blob) > 4096:
        # In unlikely case, trim strings block (should not happen with our sizes)
        blob = blob[:4096]

    return blob

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Generator for NUL-separated string list inputs suitable for fdt_stringlist_contains
# The fuzz stub consumes two FUZZ_PARAM_STR buffers:
#  - listbuf: arbitrary bytes interpreted as a NUL-separated string list with explicit length
#  - needle:  C-string to search for in the list (must be NUL-terminated when passed via c_str())
# We will return a single bytes buffer that can be split by the fuzzing harness into the
# two FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls. Since we cannot control the harness, we craft a single buffer
# that is interesting if used for either listbuf or needle. In typical setups, each
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR is sourced from the same initial seed buffer, either whole or in chunks.
# Our strategy:
#  - Construct a valid string list of multiple entries with varied characteristics
#    (empty strings, duplicates, prefixes/suffixes, unicode/UTF-8, ASCII control chars).
#  - Include entries that allow different search outcomes depending on needle:
#      * exact matches
#      * substring but not exact match (to ensure correct equality check)
#      * empty string present/absent depending on seed path
#  - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
#  - Randomize order and inclusion deterministically from seed.

ASCII_WORDS = [
    "root", "soc", "cpu", "memory", "chosen", "aliases", "serial", "i2c",
    "spi", "ethernet", "gpio", "uart", "usb", "pcie", "display", "sound",
    "firmware", "timer", "watchdog", "rng", "rtc", "thermal", "pinctrl",
]

UTF8_WORDS = [
    "μart", "spî", "éthernet", "géo", "显示", "звук", "ऑडियो", "الساعة", "タイマ", "조명",
]

SUFFIXES = [".0", ".1", "@0", "@1", "-a", "-b", "-test", "_dev", "#0", "-ctrl"]
PREFIXES = ["", "dev-", "test-", "__", "node-"]

CONTROL_FRAGMENTS = [
    "",  # allow empty string as element
    " ",
    "\t", "\n", "\r",
]


def _rand_words(rng: random.Random, count: int) -> List[str]:
    pool = ASCII_WORDS + UTF8_WORDS
    return [rng.choice(pool) for _ in range(count)]


def _maybe_mutate(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    # Create variants to test exact vs contains semantics
    ops = [
        lambda x: x,  # exact
        lambda x: x + rng.choice(SUFFIXES),
        lambda x: rng.choice(PREFIXES) + x,
        lambda x: x + "-" + x,  # repeated
        lambda x: x + str(rng.randrange(0, 10)),
    ]
    # Bias towards exacts but include variations
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return s
    return rng.choice(ops)(s)


def _build_string_list(rng: random.Random, target_size: int) -> bytes:
    # Build a list of strings joined by NUL, total size <= target_size
    entries: List[bytes] = []

    # Always include a few canonical entries to anchor behavior
    base = [
        "compatible",  # common DT property value word
        "status",      # also common
        "okay",
        "disabled",
    ]

    # Add random words and variants
    n_rand = rng.randint(5, 14)
    words = base + _rand_words(rng, n_rand)

    # Create duplicates and edge cases
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        words.append("okay")  # duplicate
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        words.append("")  # empty string element
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        words.append("\\0inside")  # literal backslash-zero text, not actual terminator
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        words.append("null\x00byte")  # include embedded NUL once we encode; will split into two entries

    # Expand and mutate
    expanded: List[str] = []
    for w in words:
        expanded.append(_maybe_mutate(rng, w))
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            expanded.append(_maybe_mutate(rng, w))
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            expanded.append(rng.choice(CONTROL_FRAGMENTS))

    # Shuffle order
    rng.shuffle(expanded)

    # Encode and pack with NUL separators
    total = 0
    for w in expanded:
        # Encode to UTF-8; replace invalids (shouldn't occur) to keep valid bytes
        b = w.encode('utf-8', 'replace')
        # If the word itself contains NUL, it effectively creates multiple list entries.
        # That's acceptable and can be interesting; we keep as-is so split by NUL happens.
        if total + len(b) + 1 > target_size:
            break
        entries.append(b)
        total += len(b) + 1

    # Guarantee at least one entry if nothing added
    if not entries:
        entries = [b"okay"]

    blob = b"\x00".join(entries)

    # Optionally end without an extra trailing NUL (both forms are acceptable)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return blob
    else:
        # Ensure there is a final NUL terminator beyond the last string
        if len(blob) + 1 <= target_size:
            return blob + b"\x00"
        return blob


def _build_needle_set(rng: random.Random, list_entries: bytes) -> List[bytes]:
    # Derive potential needles from the existing list, plus related near-misses
    parts = list_entries.split(b"\x00") if list_entries else [b""]
    needles: List[bytes] = []

    # Exact matches
    for p in parts:
        if p and p not in needles:
            needles.append(p)
            if len(needles) > 20:
                break

    # Near misses: prefix/suffix, substring, different case
    def to_str(b: bytes) -> str:
        try:
            return b.decode('utf-8', 'ignore')
        except Exception:
            return ''

    for p in parts[:10]:
        s = to_str(p)
        if not s:
            continue
        near = [
            (s + "-x").encode('utf-8'),
            ("x-" + s).encode('utf-8'),
            s.upper().encode('utf-8'),
            s.lower().encode('utf-8'),
        ]
        needles.extend(near)

    # Special needles
    needles.extend([
        b"",               # empty string
        b"nonexistent",    # guaranteed miss
        b"okay",           # common exact
        b"disabled",       # common exact
        b"status",         # common exact or near
        b"compat",         # substring of compatible
        b"\t",             # control char
    ])

    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    uniq: List[bytes] = []
    for n in needles:
        if n not in seen:
            uniq.append(n)
            seen.add(n)

    # Pick a needle deterministically
    if not uniq:
        return [b"okay"]

    rng.shuffle(uniq)
    # Return a small set; the harness will use the same buffer for both fields, so we
    # construct a combined payload with both list and one needle separated by a delimiter
    return uniq[:5]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Aim for up to 2 KB for the list, leaving room under 4096 when combined with metadata
    target_size = rng.randint(256, 2048)
    list_blob = _build_string_list(rng, target_size)

    # Build a few candidate needles; choose one deterministically
    needles = _build_needle_set(rng, list_blob)
    needle = rng.choice(needles) if needles else b"okay"

    # Compose final buffer: we include both the list and the needle so that
    # independent FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls seeded from this buffer can obtain
    # meaningful data. Use a simple header with lengths so consumers that
    # read sequentially can split, but if the harness ignores it, both
    # halves are still valid strings/lists.
    # Layout:
    #  [u32 be] list_len
    #  [list_len bytes] list_blob
    #  [u32 be] needle_len (excluding NUL terminator)
    #  [needle_len bytes] needle
    #  [NUL] explicit terminator for needle as C-string

    def be32(x: int) -> bytes:
        return struct.pack('>I', x)

    list_len = len(list_blob)
    needle_len = len(needle)

    # Ensure total size <= 4096
    header = be32(list_len) + be32(needle_len)
    max_payload = 4096 - len(header) - 1
    if list_len + needle_len > max_payload:
        # Trim deterministically from the end of list to fit
        trim = (list_len + needle_len) - max_payload
        list_blob = list_blob[:-trim] if trim < list_len else b""
        list_len = len(list_blob)
        header = be32(list_len) + be32(needle_len)

    payload = be32(list_len) + list_blob + be32(needle_len) + needle + b"\x00"
    return payload
